description:
A redo record rejects an operation set whose paths overlap, so one record cannot mean two things.

## Background

A record is applied by two mechanisms, and both must read it the same way. `4e818d10`'s code review found a record they read differently: puts at `issues/a.json` and `issues` made the in-memory backend overwrite the directory entry with a file while keeping its child, where the filesystem backend fails `EISDIR` on the rename. Both backends now refuse that record identically, discovered at apply time, because each discovers its occupants then.

The overlap itself is a property of the record alone. `835bae3f` REQ-02 already rejects a path outside the selected roots at construction; an operation set whose paths overlap is the same class of defect and is checkable in the same place, without a filesystem or a state map. Rejecting it at construction stops the divergent record existing rather than relying on two mechanisms to agree about it, and it lets `d591a1c8`'s conformance suite generate records freely instead of filtering the ones that cannot be applied.

The apply-time guards stay. They answer a different question: whether the live repository holds an occupant the record did not name. Construction-time validation answers whether the record contradicts itself.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A record is rejected at construction when one operation's path is an ancestor of another operation's path.
- [hard] REQ-02: A record is rejected at construction when two operations name the same path, including a put and a delete of it.
- [hard] REQ-03: The event append participates in both checks, so a record appending to the event log while a put or delete names that log is rejected.
- [hard] REQ-04: A record parsed from its serialized form is rejected on the same terms as one built in process, so a record that reaches a process through a file is subject to the check that built it.
- [hard] REQ-05: The rejection names both paths that overlap and which relationship they hold, so a caller can tell an ancestor conflict from a duplicate.
- [hard] REQ-06: The rejection is covered by unit tests over the record type, at the construction and parse boundaries, including a record whose paths merely share a prefix without one containing the other, which is admissible.

## Non-goals

This does not relax either backend's apply-time refusal. `35544121` and `4e818d10` both discover live occupants as they apply and must keep doing so; a record can be internally consistent and still meet a directory the repository placed at its target. This task removes a contradiction inside the record, not a conflict with the repository.

A symlink or other unsupported occupant at an operation's target remains a cross-backend difference — the filesystem backend reports `ELOOP` where the in-memory backend has no analogue to model, because it has no symlinks. That is a property of the live target rather than of the record, so construction-time validation cannot close it. It belongs to `d591a1c8`'s statement of what its conformance suite covers on each backend.

No publisher composes a record yet, so nothing in production constructs one to reject; story `21e976d1` REQ-03 holds unchanged.

## Notes

Expected footprint is roughly 30 production lines in `crates/jit/src/storage/redo_record.rs` plus its tests. The check belongs beside the root-class rejection `835bae3f` REQ-02 established, in the same constructor and the same parse path, rather than in a separate validator a caller could skip.

Raised by `4e818d10`'s worker after it fixed the apply-time divergence, and routed here rather than folded into the closed `835bae3f`.
title: A record rejects an overlapping operation set
